basis.text: Fremantle's diary of 2 July 1863 (Longstreet placing McLaws's division at 7 a.m.) and Kershaw's report of 1 October 1863 (Official Records 27/2 p. 366: the leading brigade left camp about sunrise and reached the hill overlooking Gettysburg), read with McLaws's own statement (the head of his division reached Seminary Ridge before 8 a.m.), Alexander's window (6 to 8) and Freeman's estimates (head by 6, whole division 8 to 8:30).

default.label: About 07:00: the head of McLaws's division on the ridge; the whole division up by 08:00 to 08:30

animation.note: 07:00 is the best-supported instant by which the head stands on the ridge: Fremantle's diary has Longstreet placing the division at 7 a.m. That is an upper bound reached by inference, not a documented arrival, so it is not offered as the earliest documented time. The march began about sunrise, 04:35 (Kershaw's report), from a bivouac 2 to 4 miles out, so the column is drawn marching in before 07:00; Freeman's computed 06:00 for the head stays selectable. Whether any floor moves is for the owner to decide

default.note: The head of the division is shown on the ridge at 07:00 at the latest; the plan's 08:00 and 08:30 are read as the times the whole division was up. Kershaw's brigade led the column; McLaws and Lee met on the ridge and the division then lay behind it until the march to the right (Kershaw: 'until about noon'; the hour of Lee's order is C-008's).

weighing.summary: The sources agree on an early head and differ by what they measure. A diary of the day has Longstreet placing McLaws's division at 7 a.m.; Kershaw's report has the leading brigade leaving camp about sunrise and reaching the hill overlooking Gettysburg; McLaws says the head of his division reached Seminary Ridge before 8; Freeman estimates the head by 6 and the whole division in position by 8 to 8:30. The plan's 08:00 and 08:30 are best read as the whole division up (Freeman's estimate; Longstreet's 8 a.m. of 1875 is called an error by Freeman), not the first arrival; sunrise is a later memory contradicted by Kershaw's report. Nobody gives a clock for the first arrival, so the default is an inference from the diary and the bounds.
weighing.who: Fremantle (a British officer riding with Longstreet) and Kershaw (leading brigade) wrote what they saw or did. McLaws and Longstreet were present but wrote years later (McLaws's address 1879 and an undated statement printed by Taylor in 1906; Longstreet 1875 and 1896); Hood wrote in 1875. Alexander (1907), Dickert (1899), the Meade family narrative (1913) and Freeman (1935, computed) are later accounts by writers who were behind the column, in camp, or not there.
weighing.when: Fremantle's entry is of 2 July 1863 (rank 5); Kershaw's report is dated 1 October 1863, 91 days after the event (rank 4). McLaws 1879 and the undated statement, Hood 1875, Longstreet 1875 and 1896, Alexander 1907 and Dickert 1899 are reminiscence (rank 2); the Meade narrative (1913) and Freeman (1935) are later history (rank 1). The two writings of the time outrank the rest, and the rest does not contradict them except Hood's and Longstreet's sunrise.
weighing.where: Fremantle rode over the ground with Longstreet at 7 a.m. and saw the division placed; Kershaw marched at the head of the division; McLaws rode at the head of his column and reported to Lee on the ridge, and Freeman notes that Hood and McLaws 'rode ahead of their troops', so their hours may date their own arrival; Alexander was with the reserve artillery, which reached the field about 9 a.m.; Dickert was in the brigade, in camp; the Meade narrative and Freeman were not there.
weighing.how_knew: Fremantle: eyewitness, a diary kept day by day (preface); he gives the hour and what he saw, not whether the division stood on the ridge. Kershaw: his own command; an hour for the start ('about sunrise') and none for the arrival. McLaws: eyewitness; 'early in the morning' (1879) and 'before 8 a.m.' (undated). Hood and Longstreet: memory, and Longstreet's accounts disagree (8 a.m. in 1875, sunrise in 1896; the diary has him with Lee at 5). Freeman computes from a sunrise start and a road 'little obstructed'. Alexander and the Meade narrative do not say how they knew. No writer gives a clock for the first arrival.
weighing.clock: Kershaw, McLaws, Hood, Longstreet, Alexander and Dickert wrote on the Confederate clock; Fremantle's watch is not named; Freeman and the Meade narrative state none. The difference of about 20 minutes between the armies' clocks is not applied: it is small beside the hour or more between the default and the plan's 08:00. Sunrise on 2 July is about 04:35 local mean time (the plan; Freeman gives 4:32).
weighing.independence: Groups: fremantle; kershaw (his report and his article of 1888); mclaws (his address and the statement in Taylor are one witness); freeman; alexander; longstreet-letter-1875; longstreet-1896; longstreet-report-1863; hood-letter-1875 (Longstreet printed it in 1877 and 1896, so his sunrise may rest on it); meade-1913; dickert-1899. The default rests on a diary of the day for its hour and on Kershaw, McLaws, Freeman and Alexander for the bounds; the hour 07:00 itself is stated once.
weighing.overrides: No rejected value rests on a better class of writing than the default. Read and left aside as other events: Dickert's 'the sun had long since shot its rays' (the brigade roused in camp, which Kershaw's report of 1863 contradicts); Wilcox's report of 17 July 1863 (OR 27/2 p. 617: his brigade in line at 9 a.m. as the right of the army, and McLaws's division forming line at right angles to his own at about 2 p.m., the afternoon formation); Alexander's 9 a.m. and the 7 a.m. Freeman reports for his artillery one mile west of the ridge (the artillery's arrival, not the infantry's; unfound in Alexander's own texts); Colonel Johnston's joining the head of the corps about 9 a.m., which a reply to Longstreet in the Southern Historical Society Papers vol. 5 (p. 183) states on his authority (his guiding of the march to the right, not an arrival); the night halt (Longstreet's 'a little after dark' against Kershaw's and McLaws's midnight), which rows T2-037 and T2-038 carry.

source_panel_text: About 07:00: a British officer's diary of the day has Longstreet placing McLaws's division at 7 a.m., and McLaws says his head reached the ridge before 8. The plan's 08:00 and 08:30 read as the whole division up (Freeman); a sunrise memory is contradicted by Kershaw's report. No witness gives an hour for the first arrival. Six other values stay listed.

pdf_default.note: 08:00 is when the whole division was closed up (Longstreet 1875, the Meade narrative, Freeman's 8 to 8:30), so, read as the end of the arrival (Freeman's reading of his own 8 to 8:30; he calls Longstreet's 8 a.m. an error), it may hold; it does not hold as the first arrival, which McLaws puts before 8 and a diary of the day puts at or before 7. It stays selectable.

first_delegated.note: The first pass kept 08:00 as a marked stand-in because it found no hour in the Official Records. The research found a diary of the day, Kershaw's report of the start, McLaws's own statements and Freeman's appendix, so the point is no longer a gap.

what_would_change_it: A report, letter or diary of 2 July 1863 or of the weeks after it that gives an hour for the arrival of the head or the tail of McLaws's division on Seminary Ridge (a report of Semmes's, Barksdale's or Wofford's brigade, a diary or letter of a man of the four brigades or of Cabell's battalion, McLaws's own letters of July 1863); or a source that dates the scene in which Lee and Longstreet placed McLaws's division, which McLaws describes and Fremantle's 7 a.m. may be; or an hour in the Epperson timeline that rests on a source of the time.
owner_note: The first delegated default (08:00, a marked stand-in) is replaced by an inferred value; nothing is deleted and 08:00 and 08:30 stay selectable. The floor of the arrival gate would move from 08:00 to 07:00, which a diary of the day documents for the division on the ground; Freeman's computed 06:00 and the sunrise memory are scenarios, not the floor. How the floor is reconciled is recorded by the integration step, in the open. C-005 and C-007 agree: the head of Hood's division (about 05:00) came before the head of McLaws's (by about 07:00).
